review_method: Individual contextual editorial review of stored transcript excerpts; not a human sign-off or audio verification.

cards.source_excerpt: Now, nevertheless, as the president introduces the debate series, he's now leaving the atrium.
cards.context_decision: Campus building sense, not the heart chamber or exclusively an ancient Roman courtyard. President in the source means university president.

cards.source_excerpt: But the reason that this makes the news is because, well, like I said, it's Cornell University and it's such a strange, bizarre incident with a strange conclusion.
cards.context_decision: Refers to the unusual parking-lot event, not an incidental detail.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: Singular headword corresponds to protesters in the excerpt; public opposition does not by itself imply violence.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: The transcript says rescinding student visas; preserve that attributed wording without treating it as independent legal verification.

cards.source_excerpt: He says that he was accosted in the hallway, that they continued to follow him to his car, surrounded him, banged on the windows, blocked the car, and they were shouting.
cards.context_decision: The speaker reports his claim of being accosted; the teaching example is not a quotation or evidence of that claim.

cards.source_excerpt: As well as disruptive protests resulting in the case of two individual bans from the campus.
cards.context_decision: The statement characterizes protests as disruptive; the sense is interruption, not necessarily physical destruction.

cards.source_excerpt: An automatic braking system was able to slowly maneuver my car from the parking space and exit the parking lot.
cards.context_decision: Physical vehicle movement in the quoted statement, not a political tactic.

cards.source_excerpt: And from the footage I saw, it doesn't seem that volatile.
cards.context_decision: The speaker judges the visible confrontation as not very volatile; not the chemical evaporation sense.

cards.source_excerpt: I mean, what compelled him to reverse his car when he knew that there were pedestrians, Cornell students, standing around his car?
cards.context_decision: The rhetorical source question asks what motivated reversing the car; it need not mean literal physical force.

cards.source_excerpt: It is harassment and intimidation with the direct motive of silencing speech.
cards.context_decision: An accusation in the quoted statement, not an independently established finding.

cards.source_excerpt: As the reverse lights of the vehicle were illuminated, your intentional act created a hazardous condition.
cards.context_decision: Describes the condition allegedly created near the reversing vehicle.

cards.source_excerpt: As the reverse lights of the vehicle were illuminated, your intentional act created a hazardous condition.
cards.context_decision: Literal lights-on sense in the source. Replaces a figurative example about footage revealing a detail.

cards.source_excerpt: It is harassment and intimidation with the direct motive of silencing speech.
cards.context_decision: The quoted statement alleges pressure intended to silence speech; keep attribution separate from factual endorsement.

cards.source_excerpt: He also says the behavior I experienced last night is not protest.
cards.context_decision: Noun after “is not”; distinguish protest from the misconduct alleged by the person quoted.

cards.source_excerpt: As the reverse lights of the vehicle were illuminated, your intentional act created a hazardous condition.
cards.context_decision: Source excerpt uses reverse as a modifier in reverse lights; nearby context also uses the driving verb.

cards.source_excerpt: These are the allegations against the Cornell 7 from the Jane Doe lawsuit and why it seems like everybody is divided.
cards.context_decision: Lawsuit allegations must remain attributed. Replaces the awkward translation of a separate, longer statement excerpt.

cards.source_excerpt: People are getting doxxed.
cards.context_decision: The source describes privacy exposure, not merely searching for someone. Corrects the base-form IPA that omitted the past-participle ending.

cards.source_excerpt: Because a few months later, Jane Doe will file a civil lawsuit against Cornell University and seven fraternity brothers from Cornell, now dubbed the Cornell Seven.
cards.context_decision: The source refers to a civil lawsuit and its claims, not a criminal conviction. Jane Doe is a pseudonym in that context.

cards.source_excerpt: And this was a huge scandal for Cornell earlier this year.
cards.context_decision: Refers back to the parking-lot controversy before the narration introduces later allegations.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: Plural form retained as an existing separate learning card; not removed as an exact duplicate.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: Temporary disciplinary exclusion in the list; not hanging a physical object.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: School disciplinary removal, not the bodily sense of forcing something out.

cards.source_excerpt: Big scandals of Ivy League schools punishing protesters, suspending them, expelling them, rescinding student visas.
cards.context_decision: Plural controversies concerning disciplinary responses at universities; retain distinction from the singular parking-lot reference.

cards.source_excerpt: But that will not, not even in the slightest, be the worst investigation and scandal that Cornell University will be caught up in in this year.
cards.context_decision: Superlative in the narrator’s comparison of scandals; not an assertion that any allegation has been proved.

cards.source_excerpt: Jane Doe alleges that as a student at Cornell, she went to a fraternity party where she was gang essayed for seven hours, traumatized to the point of dropping out of her dream university and her entire life has been ripped apart
cards.context_decision: Retains explicit attribution to the lawsuit; no diagnosis or independent verification is claimed.
